However there are other ways to think about this situation:

INFLATION

One of the consequences of the coronavirus outbreak is that a large number of people being quarantined and not being able to work breaks supply chains. Many goods are manufactured on a "just in time" basis, which means that the manufacturer receives the materials it requires just before it produces the end-product, saving the manufacturer on inventory costs. If the material supply is reduced or stopped then the output of the manufacturer is decreased quickly, as it has no back-up materials to maintain production in the mean-time. This reduces end-consumer supply, without also reducing demand for those goods. This scarcity drives prices of those goods up. Inflation.

Certain goods even have increased demand as people want to purchase medications, disinfectants, additional food etc.

A potential winning asset class would therefore be inflation-linked (also known as index-linked) government bonds.

Potential downside if the government response to the situation is to drive itself further into debt by spending large sums of money whilst receiving lower tax from the lower national production, may eventually cause the government to default on the bonds.

INDUSTRY SPECIFIC EQUITIES

Pharmaceuticals and chemical manufacturers will have increased demand for their goods, and are likely to be keen (perhaps mandated by governments) to maintain production, this may cause these companies' stocks to rise. Alternatively you could purchase corporate bonds for these specific companies.

SHORT EVERYTHING
